title: Rights holders analysis of educational accountability for displaced children in Bishan Gurracha Ethiopia
text_snippet: Rights holders analysis of educational accountability for displaced children in Bishan Gurracha Ethiopia Abstract This study investigates educational interventions for internally displaced (IDP) children in Bishan Gurracha, Ethiopia, through the dual lenses of Katarina Tomasevski’s 4A’s Framework and the New Sociology of Childhood. Moving beyond a descriptive account of resource shortages, the research theorises a “Sociology of Neglect” based on the lived experiences of children as active social agents. Employing qualitative narrative design and an exploratory qualitative approach, the study engaged 16 purposively sampled IDP children (9 of them female) to co-construct accounts of their educational experiences. Data gathered via semi-structured interviews and field observations were analysed using thematic analysis. The findings reveal a systemic “rights-gap” characterised by “Hollow availability,” where duty bearers provide structural availability while failing to ensure economic accessibility, acceptability and adaptability of the learning environment. This results in linguistic dispossession and functional exclusion. title: Perceived competency development as a pathway to lecturer retention intention in Indonesian private nursing higher education
text_snippet: Perceived competency development as a pathway to lecturer retention intention in Indonesian private nursing higher education Abstract Lecturer retention intention is a critical educational management concern in Indonesian private nursing higher education because it affects teaching continuity, clinical supervision, academic coordination, and program reliability. However, limited research has explained how institutional conditions are associated with lecturer retention intention through perceived competency development. This study examines whether perceived competency development mediates the relationships of technology satisfaction and perceived organizational support with lecturer retention intention in Indonesian private nursing higher education. Using a cross-sectional survey of 248 lecturers, the data were analyzed using PLS-SEM with bootstrapping to estimate direct, indirect, and total effects. The results show that perceived competency development was positively associated with lecturer retention intention (β = 0.516), and perceived organizational support was indirectly associated with lecturer retention intention through perceived competency development (β = 0.200). title: Teacher authority, responsibility, and platform governance in generative AI-supported classrooms
text_snippet: Teacher authority, responsibility, and platform governance in generative AI-supported classrooms Abstract Public debate on large language models (LLMs) in education often asks whether artificial intelligence will replace teachers. This article argues that this question misses a more important shift: in postdigital classrooms, teachers’ authority is not disappearing but being reorganized. As generative AI reduces the centrality of teachers’ authority based on knowledge possession, teachers are increasingly expected to exercise three other forms of authority: epistemic-arbitration authority, pedagogical-orchestration authority, and normative-accountability authority. They must judge the reliability of AI outputs, decide when and how AI should be used, and uphold standards of fairness, academic integrity, public reasoning, and student safety. Drawing on recent scholarship on teacher agency, professional judgement, AI literacy, assessment, responsible AI, and platform governance, the article argues that this shift is accompanied by a downward transfer of responsibility. title: Nature-based solutions in built environment education for developing sustainability competencies through bibliometric and systematic analysis
text_snippet: Nature-based solutions in built environment education for developing sustainability competencies through bibliometric and systematic analysis Abstract Nature-based Solutions (NbS) are increasingly recognized for their potential to address complex urban sustainability challenges; however, their integration into higher education curricula within built environment disciplines remains fragmented. This study examines how NbS contribute to the development of professional sustainability competencies and identifies pedagogical strategies most effective for embedding NbS in built environment education. A mixed-methods design was adopted, combining bibliometric analysis of 919 publications (2015–2025) with a systematic review of 26 peer-reviewed studies. The PRISMA framework guided study selection and screening, ensuring methodological rigor and transparency. The bibliometric analysis maps research trends, knowledge structures and thematic developments, while the systematic review evaluates pedagogical approaches and their impact on student learning outcomes. Results reveal six major clusters of teaching strategies and six corresponding competency domains. text_snippet: Perceived digital competence following virtual reality-supported physics learning in junior secondary schools Abstract Virtual reality-supported physics learning is increasingly recognized as a promising approach for strengthening both science understanding and digital competence in school settings. This study described students’ perceived digital competence after participation in virtual reality-supported solar system learning across four junior secondary schools. The observed overall mean was 3.390 (SD = 0.187), with domain means concentrated toward the upper end of the response scale. title: Fairness aware learning analytics for identifying internet induced inequality in online examinations
text_snippet: Fairness aware learning analytics for identifying internet induced inequality in online examinations Abstract Online examinations delivered through learning management systems implicitly assume stable internet connectivity — an assumption that fails systematically in infrastructure-constrained settings. In such environments, a student who loses connectivity mid-examination can be recorded identically to one who is academically unprepared, producing a measurable form of assessment inequity. This study presents a fairness-aware learning-analytics approach for identifying internet-induced inequality directly from standard examination logs. title: Developing research reasoning through digital tools in PhD students’ methodological training
text_snippet: Developing research reasoning through digital tools in PhD students’ methodological training Abstract The paper examines how digital tools integrated into the course “Modern IT in Scientific Research” are associated with patterns of research reasoning among PhD students. The authors argue that the digital transformation of science affects not only the technical aspects of a researcher’s work but may also shape how research problems are formulated, arguments are constructed, and evidence is verified. Research reasoning was operationalized through three indicators: I1—problematization, I2—methodological justification of procedures, and I3—reflective evaluation of evidence. These indicators are linked to mechanisms of digital tool use: M1—external representations and structuring of the research field (knowledge maps, citation graphs, timelines); M2—heuristic generation of alternatives and preliminary modeling; and M3—organization and verification of evidence (screening of contradictory citations, verification of claims, source management). This study presents a behavioral clustering framework that derives learner profiles from behavioral and psychological proxies and maps them to a proposed adaptive learning object recommendation framework. text_snippet: Students’ problem-solving patterns in arithmetic series tasks viewed through reflective thinking Abstract Reflective thinking plays an important role in mathematical problem-solving because it enables students to monitor their reasoning, adjust strategies, and integrate prior knowledge when confronting non-routine tasks. This study aimed to identify the problem-solving patterns students employed while engaging in reflective thinking to solve non-routine arithmetic series problems. Using a descriptive qualitative approach, research was conducted with high school students. Data was collected through non-routine mathematics problems tests on arithmetic series. The students solved the problems while thinking aloud and recorded them using audiovisual methods. Subsequently, the constant comparison method analyzed observations from answer sheets, observation sheets, and recordings. The findings revealed three distinct problem-solving patterns: Employ Variable, Visual Representation, and Direct, which reflect how students engaged reflective thinking when solving non-routine arithmetic series problems. text_snippet: A multidimensional review of artificial intelligence in science education examining trends, curriculum integration, and ethical implications Abstract Background Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into science education, yet the literature remains fragmented, lacking a unified framework that connects publication trends, curriculum implementation, and ethical considerations. Methods: A mixed-method systematic review was conducted that combined bibliometric analysis with qualitative content analysis. A total of 80 peer-reviewed studies were identified through Web of Science and Scopus databases (1990–2026) and analyzed using a structured coding scheme encompassing educational level, AI type, curriculum integration, ethical considerations, and pedagogical use. Results: Bibliometric analysis revealed an acceleration in publication growth since 2020, concentrated in higher education contexts. Qualitative analysis identified institutional and program-level integration as dominant (41%), while K-12 settings and teacher education remained underrepresented. title: Student learning experiences in challenge based learning across five Tanzanian universities
text_snippet: Student learning experiences in challenge based learning across five Tanzanian universities Abstract This paper examines how innovative pedagogical models can support quality learning within resource-constrained higher education, contributing to inclusive and transformative education. The study examined students’ experiences, outcomes, and participation barriers through the Multi-competence Learning (MCL) programme, a locally adapted form of the Challenge-Based Learning (CBL) approach implemented across five Tanzanian universities. A mixed-methods analysis of surveys and group interviews from 226 students shows that MCL enhanced technical proficiency with geospatial tools, systems thinking, agency, and collaborative problem-solving. Students also reported that the community-linked challenges and stakeholders’ input, increased sense of purpose and belonging, motivation, and confidence in applying theory to practice. Concurrently, they reported challenges they faced, such as limited access to Information and Communication Technologies, heavy workloads, uneven mentorship, and difficulties obtaining datasets, which influenced participation and learning depth. title: Why educational change accumulates rather than replaces in Ukrainian natural science education from 1950 to 2022
text_snippet: Why educational change accumulates rather than replaces in Ukrainian natural science education from 1950 to 2022 Abstract Educational change theory commonly assumes that reforms replace what came before: outdated curricula give way to modern ones, teacher-centered pedagogy yields to student-centered approaches, and ideological content is displaced by scientific objectivity. We argue that this replacement assumption describes the trajectory of post-Soviet educational reform poorly. Drawing on a documentary corpus of 393 catalogued items spanning seven decades of Ukrainian natural science education (1950–2022), of which 101 are primary legislative, archival and curricular documents, we show that successive reforms—Soviet polytechnicalization, post-independence nationalization, and European competency-based frameworks—did not displace their predecessors. Formal structures established under one settlement persisted alongside those introduced by the next, producing a palimpsest in which older arrangements remain legible beneath newer policy language. text_snippet: Vocational education for entrepreneurial career transformation in the construction sector Abstract Aim This article examines how Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) can support entrepreneurial career transformation among workers in the construction sector. text_snippet: Meta-synthesis of global cases for the adaption stages of artificial intelligence systems into university practices Abstract The transformative potential of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in universities is simply extending beyond instructional applications to include administrative and strategic domains in university management. title: Virtual reality and gamification for STEM learning among speech impaired learners in Ghana
text_snippet: Virtual reality and gamification for STEM learning among speech impaired learners in Ghana Abstract Virtual reality (VR) and gamification are increasingly used in STEM education to enhance student engagement and learning. However, it remains unclear how these technologies address the needs of students with speech impairments, particularly in low-resource settings in Ghana. This scoping review examines existing research on the use of VR and gamification in inclusive STEM education, with a specific focus on accessibility features and the representation of speech-impaired learners in the literature. Using PRISMA-ScR guidelines, 2501 records were identified from five databases. After screening, 40 studies published between 2020 and 2024 were included. However, very few studies explicitly address accessibility for learners with speech impairments, and only a small number consider low-resource or marginalized educational contexts. Most of the existing research originates from high-income countries and tends to focus on broader disability groups rather than on speech impairment as a distinct category.

This study examines how the geometry of façade openings relates to high-school students’ emotional responses, with a particular focus on forms associated with the golden ratio and Iranian proportional systems. We hypothesised that hexagonal openings, rooted in the Iranian proportional tradition, would be associated with more positive emotional appraisals than openings based on the conventional golden-ratio rectangle, the golden triangle, or strongly elongated rectangles. A semantic differential questionnaire using a seven-point Likert scale was administered to third-grade female high-school students in Babol, Iran ( n = 327), across three study tracks (mathematics, experimental sciences, and humanities) and two school types (public and private). title: Peer comment wording in pre-service teacher microteaching tracks rating severity but not the dimensions rated low
text_snippet: Peer comment wording in pre-service teacher microteaching tracks rating severity but not the dimensions rated low Abstract In microteaching peer evaluation, pre-service teachers often give each peer both numerical ratings and a short written comment. This study asks whether the explicit content of those comments corresponds to the evaluator’s own ratings, both overall and for specific rated items. We analyzed 702 peer evaluations from a single Japanese cohort (27 pre-service teachers, each rating 26 peers; self-evaluations excluded). Each evaluation paired nine forced-distribution ratings, treated as within-evaluator relative ranks, with one short Japanese comment. Using a fixed rule-based lexicon, we measured five explicit comment markers (generic praise, concrete instructional referent, learner-oriented mention, feed-forward, and criticism) and related them to the ratings with within-evaluator permutation tests. Generic praise was common (67.1%), whereas explicit feed-forward and criticism were rare (about 13–14% and 5–6% of comments). title: Extending the affective process and strategic engagement framework to address writer’s block in Ethiopian English as a foreign language contexts through critical artificial intelligence literacy and ethical generative artificial intelligence in low-resource settings
text_snippet: Extending the affective process and strategic engagement framework to address writer’s block in Ethiopian English as a foreign language contexts through critical artificial intelligence literacy and ethical generative artificial intelligence in low-resource settings Abstract Writer’s block remains a serious obstacle for undergraduate English as foreign language writers, particularly in low-resource Global South settings, where writing anxiety, linguistic insecurity, and unreliable internet access intensify the challenge. Researchers have shown growing interest in generative artificial intelligence tools such as ChatGPT as writing support resources, yet existing scholarship has not yet explained how EFL learners in such settings engage with these tools critically and purposefully. This study asked three questions. How do undergraduate EFL writers at a public university in Ethiopia use generative AI to manage writer’s block? What does that engagement reveal about their development of critical AI literacy? The researcher conducted an interpretive multiple case study with ten undergraduate students at Bahir Dar University across one academic semester. title: Integration of ChatGPT to enhance English speaking skills among secondary school students in Pakistan
text_snippet: Integration of ChatGPT to enhance English speaking skills among secondary school students in Pakistan Abstract The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into education is expanding rapidly, particularly in language learning. This study evaluated the effectiveness of a ChatGPT-assisted learning module in enhancing English-speaking proficiency in terms of range, accuracy, fluency, interaction, and coherence among secondary school students. A pre-test-post-test control group experimental design was employed, involving fifty Grade 9 students from a public school who were randomly assigned to experimental and control groups. English-speaking proficiency was assessed before and after the intervention through monologue and dialogue speaking tests using the Common European Framework of Reference (CEFR) rubric. The experimental group received a 12-week ChatGPT-assisted learning module in which ChatGPT was integrated to provide interactive speaking practice through voice- and text-based conversations with feedback, whereas the control group received traditional instruction. title: Examining systems thinking through a biopsychosocial and cultural perspective in engineering education
text_snippet: Examining systems thinking through a biopsychosocial and cultural perspective in engineering education Abstract Engineering education often prioritizes technical aspects over the systematic integration of social, cultural, and biological dimensions, guiding a consistent development of engineering solutions that may transform sociocultural contexts. To address this gap, this study examines the implementation of a systemic perspective based on the Biopsychosocial and Cultural Model within a capstone engineering course. The study explores how this perspective shapes students’ projects and instructors’ practices, offering insights into multidimensional integration in engineering education. It follows an Educational Design-Based Research approach within a constructivist lens and incorporates a Self-Study of Teaching Practice methodology to document and analyze instructors’ experiences, reflections, decisions, and strategies during the course. During implementation, instructors guided the student teams in project development and recorded observations, experiences, and insights in reflective journals. title: Mapping generative AI governance readiness in Kurdistan Region universities
text_snippet: Mapping generative AI governance readiness in Kurdistan Region universities Abstract Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is reshaping higher education by challenging established ideas of plagiarism, authorship, academic integrity, assessment, disclosure, digital literacy, and institutional responsibility. Many universities already have plagiarism or academic-misconduct policies, but these policies may not be sufficient for guiding the educational use of tools such as ChatGPT and other GenAI systems. This study examines public-facing GenAI readiness across a 30-university audit sample in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq. Using website-based document analysis, it assesses publicly available evidence across 11 dimensions: plagiarism policy, academic integrity guidance, GenAI guidance, acceptable and unacceptable AI use, AI-use disclosure, assessment redesign, student AI literacy, staff guidance, privacy and data protection, institutional governance, and Kurdish/local-language accessibility. A descriptive survey design was adopted, drawing data from final-year Business Education students in the two public universities in the state through a structured questionnaire. text_snippet: Determinants of continuance intention toward eLearning usage in higher education institutions Abstract This study aims to examine the key determinants influencing students’ continuance intention towards eLearning usage in higher education institutions in Iraq. It proposes an integrated model combining the Expectation-Confirmation Model (ECM) and the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology 2 (UTAUT2), extended with the construct of digital literacy. This study also addresses a critical gap in the literature related to technology continuance in developing countries like Iraq, where systemic challenges persist. A quantitative approach was adopted, and data were collected from 332 students in public universities using a structured questionnaire. text_snippet: Individual differences in digital literacy and learner profiles among higher education students Abstract Higher education (HE) is undergoing a digital revolution with the development and application of key digital skills a ubiquitous requirement for teaching, learning, and assessment opportunities. text_snippet: Generative artificial intelligence use for academic writing in English among Kuwaiti nursing and health sciences students in a mixed methods study Abstract Research on generative AI use in EMI nursing and health sciences contexts in the Gulf region remains limited. title: Effects of AI-assisted speaking practice on spoken English performance in higher vocational education
text_snippet: Effects of AI-assisted speaking practice on spoken English performance in higher vocational education Abstract With the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI), AI-assisted tools are increasingly integrated into language education. Post-intervention speaking performance was assessed by three trained raters using an analytic rubric covering pronunciation, language use, fluency and coherence, and interaction. text_snippet: Fostering multidimensional thinking in chemistry education through an integrated challenge-based learning model with socioscientific issues and counterargumentation Abstract Multidimensional thinking, comprising critical, creative, and caring thinking, is important for chemistry learning involving authentic challenges, socioscientific issues (SSI), and counterargumentation (CA). This quasi-experimental study compared the Challenge-Socioscientific Issues-Counterargumentation (CHASICA) learning model with Problem-Based Learning (PBL) model among 300 Grade 12 students from four public high schools in Bali, Indonesia. Intact classes completed pretest and posttest measures of critical, creative, and caring thinking over ten learning sessions. The instruments were developed from established theoretical frameworks, reviewed by experts, and demonstrated acceptable internal consistency. Posttest outcomes were analyzed by controlling for prior abilities, with interaction terms included where the relationship between pretest and posttest scores differed across groups. title: A qualitative typology of teachers’ orientations toward artificial intelligence integration in Lebanese schools
text_snippet: A qualitative typology of teachers’ orientations toward artificial intelligence integration in Lebanese schools Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly reshaping educational practices, requiring teachers to develop new competencies while navigating complex ethical considerations. This qualitative study explores the perceptions, practices, and orientations of 28 Lebanese schoolteachers regarding the integration of AI in school settings. Findings indicate that while a majority of participants reported familiarity with AI, only a limited proportion integrated AI into their instructional practices. Reported barriers included insufficient training, lack of institutional support, and concerns related to data privacy and ethical use. The analysis led to the identification of three qualitative orientations toward AI integration—reluctant users, early adopters, and critical skeptics—reflecting differentiated levels of readiness and engagement. The findings highlight the need for context-sensitive, pedagogically grounded, and ethically informed professional development to support sustainable AI integration in education.

title: Cybersecurity risk profiles of undergraduate students in platform dependent higher education
text_snippet: Cybersecurity risk profiles of undergraduate students in platform dependent higher education Abstract As higher education becomes increasingly organised through multi-platform digital learning ecosystems, students’ cybersecurity practices have become part of everyday academic participation. However, cybersecurity education often treats students as a uniform risk group and assumes that greater awareness leads to safer behaviour. This study challenges that assumption by identifying distinct cybersecurity risk profiles among undergraduate students. Survey data were collected from 372 undergraduate students at a public university in Ghana and analysed using latent profile analysis, chi-square tests and binary logistic regression. Four profiles emerged: low-exposure low-risk, digitally engaged protected, aware-but-vulnerable, and moderate baseline. The aware-but-vulnerable profile was the most theoretically important group, combining above-average social media use, high cybersecurity awareness and high cybersecurity vulnerability.
